title: Out of memory on Firefox and Chrome from Grafana 9.5.20 to 11.2.2 and later
body: I have 32 GB of memory, an Intel Core i7-10700, and Windows 11 Pro 23H2. After loading a fairly complex dashboard with 30 panels in Grafana 11.2.2 and scrolling about halfway down, the dashboard freezes and both Chrome and Firefox show a browser out-of-memory error. Windows Task Manager reaches 98% memory usage, then returns to 15% after I close the Grafana tab; CPU usage remains stable. I have tried multiple newer Grafana versions and always reverted to 9.5.20 because it works, while the issue form also lists docker 9.5.2.0 as having worked before. The Docker dashboard uses varied Prometheus and InfluxDB sources. This is a browser-tab error rather than an error inside one panel, and no corresponding error appears in the Grafana log.

symptoms_visible: After I load the 30-panel dashboard and scroll about halfway down, the Grafana tab freezes and both Chrome and Firefox display an out-of-memory error.
Windows memory usage reaches 98% and returns to about 15% when I close the Grafana tab; CPU usage stays stable and the Grafana log shows no error.
N0.label: N0 browser out-of-memory reported

symptoms_visible: The 11.2.2 browser tab still freezes after I scroll through the dashboard, so its HAR only covers the initial load before scrolling.
N1.label: N1 sanitized dashboard and network artifacts supplied

symptoms_visible: After I removed the two panels that use the inner-join transformation, the dashboard loaded without the browser running out of memory on the latest Grafana Docker release.
N2.label: N2 dashboard loads with join panels removed

symptoms_visible: I pulled Grafana 12.1, but the panels using inner join still would not open; the same panels came up immediately in a separate Grafana 9.5.2.0 instance.
N3_x.label: N3_x Grafana 12.1 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: I inserted a Group by transformation in the panel under Grafana 9.5.2.0, saved it, and imported it into 12.1, but the panel still would not open.
N4_x.label: N4_x generic Group by attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: The join panel still will not open with my earlier Group by setup; I have supplied debug dashboards containing its data for reproduction.
N5.label: N5 reduced panel debug data collected

symptoms_visible: Once I configured Calculate Last for the values in the Group by transformation and used the revised transformation sequence, the panel opened and the transforms worked the way I wanted.
N_terminal.label: terminal panel works with pre-join aggregation

question_patterns: Can you share the dashboard JSON and sanitized HAR files from a working and affected version?
Could you provide an exported dashboard and a browser network capture that we can use to investigate?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached the dashboard JSON and sanitized HAR files. The 11.2.2 HAR is only from the initial browser load before scrolling, because scrolling is what freezes the browser; the other HAR is from the working 9.5.20 version.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I exported the dashboard, and it contains no transformations or joins; a one-panel dashboard with a single query has the same memory behavior.
I supplied the same dashboard JSON and captures after sanitizing them with a different tool.

edges.comment: Thread c1-c5, reporter's system only: support requested dashboard and HAR artifacts; the reporter sanitized and uploaded them, while explaining why the affected-version capture ends before scrolling.

solution.intent: Use the supplied dashboard to isolate the immediate trigger, then temporarily remove the two panels containing the inner joinByField transformation so the rest of the dashboard remains usable.
solution.concrete_example: The exported dashboard contains an inner joinByField using ifName. Remove or disable the two panels using that transform and reload the dashboard to see whether memory remains stable.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter uploaded the dashboard but did not initially identify its joinByField block. Reading the JSON and associating that transformation with the failing panels is engineer-side analysis.

edges.comment: Thread c6-c9, reporter's dashboard and system: a participant found the inner joinByField block in the reporter's JSON; the reporter removed the two affected panels and confirmed that the remaining dashboard loaded. This is a successful but functionality-reducing workaround, not the final resolution.

solution.intent: Upgrade to Grafana 12.1 and retry the original inner-join panels on the assumption that the newer join performance work resolves their memory failure.
solution.concrete_example: Pull Grafana 12.1, restore or open the panels that use inner join, and check whether they now load.

edges.comment: Thread c11-c17, reporter's system only: after a maintainer suggested trying Grafana 12.1, the reporter pulled that release and found that the original inner-join panels still would not open. The separate 9.5.2.0 comparison was a diagnostic instance; participant2's separate five-table deployment is not merged into this causal chain.

solution.intent: Add a generic Group by transformation before the join without fully configuring how the non-key value fields should be reduced.
solution.concrete_example: Insert a Group by transformation ahead of the inner join, save the panel, and import it into Grafana 12.1.

edges.comment: Thread c16-c17 and later clarification in c28, reporter's panel only: the reporter inserted Group by and imported the saved panel into 12.1, but it still would not open. The reporter only disclosed after the successful configuration that this earlier attempt omitted Calculate Last, so that omission is not exposed at this node.

question_patterns: Can you export a panel debug dashboard that includes the data needed to reproduce this panel?
Could you use the panel debugging export so the join can be investigated with the actual data?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached one of my panels with its diagnostic data as POEPanel.json.zip.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I exported the panel with its data, and every value in the field used for joining is unique in every frame.

question_patterns: Can you reduce the time range to the smallest data set that still reproduces the panel problem and upload it again?
The first debug export is very large; could you send a smaller reproducer with the data retained?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This smaller debug dashboard should work. It has about 100 data points.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I reduced it to about 120 data points instead, and it still reproduces the same panel behavior.
I renamed the exported zip file before uploading it, but its dashboard and data are unchanged.

edges.comment: Thread c18-c19 and c25-c26, reporter's panel and data: maintainers requested a panel debug dashboard, then a smaller version because the first export was 57 MB. The reporter supplied both, including the reduced roughly 100-point reproducer.

solution.intent: Keep the modern SQL-style join behavior and prevent duplicate join values from multiplying rows: aggregate each join group first, calculate the last non-null value for each value field, then join and perform human-readable field organization afterward.
solution.concrete_example: In this panel, Group by the name and alias fields, set every Value field to Calculate Last non-null, then Join by name. Finally use Organize Fields by Name for readable column names instead of relying on field-override renaming during the earlier transformations. Reload the panel and verify that it opens and produces the intended table.
solution.inference_hint: From the reporter's debug data, the maintainer reduced the case to four five-row frames and observed 625 output rows in the current implementation versus one row in 9.5.2. They then confirmed with a SQL sandbox that repeated keys produce standard many-to-many join multiplication. The maintainer also determined that the panel's field-override renaming happens only after all transformations. Those conclusions are engineer analysis; the reporter supplied the data and later confirmed that Calculate Last made the proposed sequence work.

edges.comment: Thread c20-c28, reporter's panel chain: maintainers reproduced combinatorial join growth using a reduced derivative of the reporter's data, retained SQL-style join semantics, and reworked the reporter's panel with Group by plus Last non-null before Join and Organize Fields afterward. In c28 the reporter confirmed on their own panel that this configuration worked and explained that their failed attempt had omitted Calculate Last. Other users' Azure or five-table setups are not folded into this resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the modern inner join follows SQL-style many-to-many semantics, so duplicate values in the join field multiply matching rows combinatorially and can exhaust the browser's memory.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the supplied dashboard and panel debug data, including the reduced reproduction showing that current join behavior expands repeated-key frames, rather than being asserted from the out-of-memory symptom alone.

The working panel configuration must aggregate before joining: Group by the join identity, calculate the Last or Last non-null value for the value fields, then perform the join and organize or rename fields afterward.

Must not claim that upgrading to Grafana 12.1 alone fixes the issue, and must not present an unconfigured generic Group by transform as sufficient; both were tried on the reporter's panel without making it open.
Removing the two join panels may be offered only as a temporary workaround, not as the complete resolution.
Must ask the reporter to verify the reworked panel and treat the case as resolved only after the reporter confirms that it opens and produces the intended result.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Grafana administrator using Docker, Prometheus, InfluxDB, browser diagnostics, dashboard JSON exports, and multiple Grafana test instances; able to edit transformation pipelines when given precise instructions.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and persistent, with detailed environment observations and practical test results. Challenges incomplete explanations politely, supplies requested sanitized artifacts, and clearly distinguishes a workaround from a satisfactory panel configuration.
